possession.modeDuoMeta: Taking turns, or each on your own phone
possession.relaisDebut: Answer all the questions, then pass the phone.
possession.relaisSuite: {{nom}} is done. Your turn, no peeking at their answers!
possession.verdictEquivalent: Two different answers, the same fate.
possession.ecartsTitre: Where you didn't react the same way
possession.modesDesc: Ten days in a house whose story nobody wants to tell. Solo, you find out your risk. As a couple, each of you answers separately, and we find out who opens the door to the demons.
possession.modeSoloDesc: Fifteen questions, a risk in percent.
possession.modeDuoDesc: Taking turns on the same phone, or each on your own with remote mode.
possession.setupDescSolo: Ten days in a cheap house whose story nobody wants to tell: the Ouija board in the attic, the mirror from the flea market, the voice that knows your first name. Fifteen questions, a possession risk as a percentage, with what protects you and what exposes you.
possession.setupTitreDuo: Which of you could get possessed?
possession.setupDescDuo: Enter your first names. The first player answers the fifteen questions, passes the phone, and the second answers in turn. At the end, your two risks side by side, and the name of the one the demons would choose.
possession.duoPerd: {{nom}} is the one who gets possessed, at {{vp}}. {{autre}} gets away with {{va}}.
possession.duoEgal: Same risk for both of you: {{v1}}. The demon will have to choose.
possession.verdictDifferent: {{nom}} opens the door a little wider.
possession.noteFin: A Halloween quiz, just for fun. No demons were consulted in writing it.
possession.r1_d: You lock the doors, you refuse Ouija boards, you sleep with the duvet up to your chin. Demons move on: too much work for too little.
possession.r1_a: Keep it up. And keep a bit of salt on you, for the others.
possession.r2_d: You have the right reflexes, but you can't help looking. A demon would really have to work to get in, and it has other houses to visit.
possession.r2_a: Avoid filming doors that slam. Close them.
possession.r3_d: On a normal day, you're fine. On a tired night, in an old house, with a Ouija board lying around... that's debatable.
possession.r3_a: Sleep well, especially in October. And leave the board in the attic.
possession.r4_d: You talk to mirrors, you go downstairs when the voice calls you, and you bring home flea-market finds without asking questions. Demons pass your address around.
possession.r4_a: Before buying an old object, at least ask where it comes from.
possession.r5_d: Honestly, we wonder whether it's you taking this quiz or whether something is doing it in your place. You open every door, you say yes to everything, and you find it funny.
possession.r5_a: If your eyes turn completely black while reading this result, let someone know.
possession.q1: The house is old, cheap, and the estate agent won't say why the last occupants left.
possession.q1a: I sign right away: a house with a history, that's the dream
possession.q1b: I sign, but I ask the neighbour for the story that same evening
possession.q1c: I ask to see the cellar and the attic first, with a torch
possession.q1d: A house whose history nobody will tell, that's a no, even at that price
possession.q2: In the attic, under a sheet: a Ouija board, the glass already sitting on it.
possession.q2a: We're playing tonight, it's a sign!
possession.q2b: I look at it from a distance, curious, and photograph it for my friends
possession.q2c: I leave it under the sheet and don't go up to the attic again
possession.q2d: I burn it in the garden, glass included
possession.q3a: Arms spread wide, window open, door ajar 'for the cat'
possession.q3b: One foot sticking out of the duvet, hallway light off
possession.q3c: On my side, a night light on, door shut
possession.q3d: Door locked, duvet up to my chin, a torch under the pillow
possession.q4: The neighbour tells you, without smiling: 'This house is lived in, you know. Not by you.'
possession.q4a: 'Brilliant! Which room is the most lived in?'
possession.q4b: 'So I hear, but I don't really believe it', and I go inside
possession.q4c: I go round the rooms with salt, just in case
possession.q4d: I ask him for the previous owner's number and sleep at a hotel tonight
possession.q5: The bedroom door slams by itself. Three times. There's no draught.
possession.q5a: I go and look, asking the house 'is that you?'
possession.q5b: I film it for social media, with creepy music
possession.q5c: I put a wedge in, check the windows, and tell myself it's the wood settling
possession.q5d: I say 'not tonight' out loud and go and sleep at a friend's
possession.q6: On a stall, an old oval mirror. The seller doesn't want to be paid, he just wants it gone.
possession.q6a: I take it and hang it above the bed
possession.q6b: I take it for the hallway, it's pretty
possession.q6c: I ask where it comes from, and I leave it
possession.q6d: A seller giving away a mirror, that's a no; I move on to the next stall
possession.q7: A very soft voice asks you to come down to the cellar. It knows your first name.
possession.q7a: I go down, it sounded nice
possession.q7b: I ask it what it wants, from the top of the stairs
possession.q7c: I put my earphones in at full volume and sleep with the light on
possession.q7d: I leave the house in my pyjamas, and put it up for sale tomorrow
possession.q8: The cat is staring at the corner of the living room, back arched, hissing. There's nothing in the corner.
possession.q8a: I go into the corner and say 'boo' to relax him
possession.q8b: I take a photo of the corner, to see if there's a shape
possession.q8c: I pick up the cat and change rooms
possession.q8d: I follow the cat: he leaves, I leave
possession.q9: A priest rings the bell: he was 'passing by' and offers to bless the house, just in case.
possession.q9a: I laugh and close the door
possession.q9b: I ask him to leave the bottle of holy water, for later
possession.q9c: I ask what it involves first, and I accept
possession.q9d: I accept, and ask him to come back every week
possession.q10: In the housewarming photos, there's one extra person. In the background. In all of them.
possession.q10a: I zoom in, find her quite nice-looking, and post the photo
possession.q10b: I show the photos to everyone to find out who it is
possession.q10c: I delete the photos and change my phone's password
possession.q10d: I sleep somewhere else and call the priest who was passing by
possession.q11: These days, honestly, you'd say you're...
possession.q11a: At rock bottom: exhaustion, break-up, work, all at once
possession.q11d: On top of the world, nothing gets to me, least of all a house
possession.q12: You wake up speaking a language you don't know. Someone recorded it.
possession.q12a: I listen to it on repeat, I find it pretty, I learn the sentence
possession.q12b: I look up the translation online; it's Latin, apparently
possession.q12c: I send the recording to the priest
possession.q12d: I'm already at the hotel with my suitcases; the house can keep the sentence
possession.q13a: Taken part in a séance, and I was the one asking the questions
possession.q13b: Slept in a cemetery, for a laugh
possession.q13c: Visited a haunted house, in a group, in broad daylight
possession.q13d: None of that, and I intend to keep it that way
possession.q14: In the abandoned church at the end of the lane, a statue is looking at you. It has no eyes.
possession.q14a: I talk to it, and tell it about my week
possession.q14b: I go closer to touch it
possession.q14c: I take the photo and leave
possession.q14d: I leave without looking back, and I don't come back
possession.q15a: I always say yes, to everything, to everyone
possession.q15c: I don't believe in anything, so nothing can get to me... normally
possession.q15d: I'm stubborn: nobody makes me do anything, not even a demon
